source: Nicolas Balzamo, « Uniformisation ou distinction ? Le couronnement des Madones dans l'Europe moderne (XVIIe-XVIIIe siècles) », Réforme, Humanisme, Renaissance 97 (2023), pp. 169-190. Coronations named in the text and footnotes, with his citations of BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate (volume, folio) where given.
note: SECONDARY: reported by the article, not read here. Rows with a folio citation are `medium`; rows he gives as a bare year in prose (the Sicilian and Piedmontese lists, the Naples list) are `low` and carry no folio. Images he names only by town are recorded by town with the title null.

rows.subject: Blessed Virgin Mary
rows.notes: The first image crowned under the Sforza initiative, before the count's earliest surviving letters of 1634 (p. 174); 1631 is the year of the petition per Vrabelová 2013, p. 59. Re-crowned by the Chapter in 1697 (see the tomo IV dossier).

rows.subject: Blessed Virgin Mary
rows.notes: One of the first crowned after Sforza's death; the nuns' letter claimed the icon was begun by St Luke and finished by God.

rows.subject: Blessed Virgin Mary

rows.notes: Chapter's assent 1696, ceremony 8 June 1704; the canon brought the crown from Rome and placed it after a sung Mass, the local bishop assisting. Resolves the OCR-garbled surname in the tomo IV dossier.

rows.subject: Blessed Virgin Mary
rows.notes: NOT EXECUTED. Petitioned by Lorenzo Boturini (memorial of 18 July 1738); the Chapter agreed, but the Council of the Indies annulled the coronation and expelled Boturini (citing Escamilla González 2010). The image was first crowned in 1895. Corrects the reading of Vrabelová 2013, p. 62, that the Chapter 'crowned' it on 1 October 1740.
